fixes.title: Fix: Unclear escalation loop
fixes.summary: 3 failing runs graded by jev-demo-decision-failure. Evidence: “Escalated later by a different team; root cause unclear.”.

corrective_entry.value:
Risk: Unclear escalation loop in review notes.
Evidence:
- Failing run 83b903a2: review text "Escalated later by a different team; root cause unclear." (also the live lesson at jev-demos/lead_routing/team3b-s11/senselab/learned-mid-market-emea-5b6fddc3@v35) and judge note: "Escalated later by a different team; root cause unclear."
- Failing run ff9759f7: review text "Went badly for reasons outside the decision; flagged by the reviewing team." (read @v31 of the same entry).
- Passing run af0ec625: review text "Partner closed the deal in 30 days." (read @v33), which is clear and validated.
Problem: The agent echoed vague, non-causal escalation notes from a learned entry (worked=false, low confidence, discredited in these runs) as the review, causing graders to flag the outcome.
Do instead:
- Do not use lessons that state escalation by another team or "root cause unclear" or "outside the decision" as the review text.
- Prefer validated, worked=true mid_market/emea partner outcomes (e.g., "Partner closed the deal in N days.") when available.
- If only ambiguous or non-causal notes are available, give a neutral rationale for the decision (e.g., "Decision: partner per mid_market/emea playbook and intent"), and avoid attributing outcomes.
Scope: Applies when the learned-mid-market-emea-5b6fddc3 text contains phrases like "Escalated later by a different team" or "Went badly for reasons outside the decision" or when the entry has low confidence/discredited evidence.

manifest.rationale: The failing runs echo vague escalation notes as the review despite successful tool calls. Run 83b903a2 reads jev-demos/lead_routing/team3b-s11/senselab/learned-mid-market-emea-5b6fddc3@v35 (discredited) with text: "Escalated later by a different team; root cause unclear." and responds: "review: Escalated later by a different team; root cause unclear." The judge flags: "Escalated later by a different team; root cause unclear." Run ff9759f7 reads @v31 (discredited) and responds: "Went badly for reasons outside the decision; flagged by the reviewing team." The judge mirrors this quote. In contrast, passing run af0ec625 reads @v33 and uses the validated note: "Partner closed the deal in 30 days." This shows that using ambiguous, non-causal lessons in reviews causes failure, while using validated, clear outcomes passes. A risk belief is the minimal, non-destructive change: it prevents relying on those vague entries for reviews and steers the agent to validated outcomes or neutral rationale without altering the learned entry that still supports passing runs.

corrective_entry.value: {"goal": "Always include a concise, evidence-based rationale with each lead routing decision.", "steps": ["Extract key lead attributes from the task: company size, region, industry, intent signal (e.g., pricing request, vendor evaluation), and contact role.", "Map these attributes to the known routing criteria in memory and determine the appropriate action and confidence.", "Draft the response to include both: 'decision: <action> (confidence <x>)' and 'rationale: <1\u20133 short reasons linking the attributes to the routing rules>'.", "If any critical data is missing or ambiguous, note it explicitly in the rationale and state any assumptions used."], "on_failure": "If you cannot cite at least two relevant factors or the rationale does not clearly support the chosen action, lower the confidence and state what additional information would change or firm up the decision.", "verify": "Before finalizing, ensure the response contains a 'rationale:' section and it mentions at least two concrete factors (e.g., size, region, intent) that support the chosen action."}

manifest.rationale: All three failing runs were marked by the reviewer as missing rationale: "review: Reviewer marked this one a miss; no detail recorded." (e.g., trace bce218cf-fabd-4809-992b-fa2a04482556). The tool calls succeeded (e.g., "decision recorded: partner" and "decision recorded: sdr_nurture"), so the issue is not a tool or knowledge error but the absence of an explicit rationale accompanying the decision. Adding a procedure that requires including a 'rationale:' section tied to specific lead attributes directly addresses the reviewer’s complaint.

items.name: Mismatched qualification assumptions
items.description: Agent assumes or records incorrect buyer procurement details or decision timing, causing unnecessary handoffs or outreach; leads to wasted sales effort when the prospect had different buying channels or already decided.

items.name: Unclear escalation loop
items.description: Issues resurface after initial handling and are escalated by other teams without a documented root cause, causing repeated failures and delayed resolution.

items.name: Missing rationale
items.description: Agent marks items as correct or makes decisions without providing reasoning or evidence, leaving reviewers unable to verify or reproduce the decision.

items.name: Recovered after error
items.description: A tool or step failed during the run and the agent recovered: it retried successfully, used a fallback, or told the user what went wrong.

items.name: Properly handled
items.description: The agent completed the task correctly: no judge found an unsupported claim, a missing tool call, a retry loop or an unhandled error.
